description: What an object lets a person *do*, declared once so that an item is described by its use rather than by a stat line. An item carries `affords`, drawn only from this list. It is the vocabulary in which canon is allowed to say what a thing is for.
note: **There is no word here for damage, and that is the point.** The game this canon feeds states at the top of its own guidance that combat is absent by design, and the ruling holds on this side too: canon may say a harpoon cuts, deters and is worth trading for, and canon has no way of saying it deals four. Enforcing that structurally rather than by memory is what a declared vocabulary is for -- the thirteenth value typed by accident is exactly what the lint catches, and `strike` typed by a well-meaning author six months from now is that value. If combat is ever wanted, it arrives by a deliberate edit to this file and a decision recorded in docs/decisions.md, not by an item quietly claiming it.

cut.label: Cuts
cut.note: Severs, scrapes or bores. A blade, an awl, a saw. The harpoons and spears live here, alongside the reed-knives.

bind.label: Binds
bind.note: Holds two things together. Cordage, lashing, resin glue, a pin.

carry.label: Carries
carry.note: Moves a load that hands alone could not. A basket, a yoke, a sled. Distinct from `contain`, which is about keeping rather than moving.

contain.label: Contains
contain.note: Keeps something in, and usually keeps the weather out. A jar, a skin, a lidded pot. Storage is the whole reason a grain surplus is possible, so this is a load-bearing affordance rather than a flavour one.

burn.label: Burns
burn.note: Gives heat or light. A lamp, a torch, a hearth. Varuna's oil lamp already affords exactly this in the game's kit and has since before this file existed.

deter.label: Deters
deter.note: Persuades an animal or a person to be elsewhere. A spear held level, a fire kept up, a rattle on a line. **This is the whole of what canon says about weapons in use** -- the herd moves off, and nothing was touched.

cross.label: Crosses
cross.note: Gets a person over ground they could not otherwise walk. A raft, a plank, a rope span, a pair of mud-shoes. The affordance vehicles are built out of.

mark.label: Marks
mark.note: Leaves a record. A stylus, a tally, ochre on a wall, a seal. In a game whose progression system is a diary, this is not a minor category.

trade.label: Trades
trade.note: Is wanted by somebody else. Says a thing has worth without canon committing to a price, which it should not -- there is no currency in this world and inventing one is a design decision, not a data entry.

eat.label: Eaten
eat.note: Is food. Carried on the item rather than on the material, because a raw tuber and a baked one are different objects and only one of them is dinner.

heal.label: Heals
heal.note: Treats a hurt. Salve, poultice, bitter tonic. Canon-side only: the game has no health to restore and reads this as description, not as a mechanic.

shelter.label: Shelters
shelter.note: Keeps weather off a sleeping person. Matting, a hide tent, a bedroll -- which the game's kit has carried from its first step.
